ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part II.1; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss 21.1-21.4 (Individuals with Significant Control Register); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 10. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent corporate registrar in the shareholder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issued by a Hague Convention Contracting State; otherwise Consular Legalization at the issuing country's foreign mission for use in Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport bio-data page of each director, officer and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public, commissioner of oaths, or equivalent public authority in the jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the notarial certificate if the jurisdiction is a Hague Contracting State; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney executed by each non-resident shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner authorizing Quebec incorporation and banking arrangements
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent legal authority in the jurisdiction of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if executed in a Hague Contracting State; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and proof of address for each foreign ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank in the beneficial owner's country of residence, validated under local AML/CFT procedures
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized bank letter with Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization where the registry or Canadian financial institution insists on certification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate or criminal record attestation for each foreign director and ultimate beneficial owner where legally available
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or competent criminal record authority in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable; French certified translation required for Quebec filings

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation of all non-French due-diligence documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified translator licensed under the Quebec Charter of the French Language and recognized by the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interprètes agréés du Québec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required for the translation certificate itself; underlying source documents remain subject to apostille or consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, officers, ultimate beneficial owners, counterparties and authorized representative(s) must be screened against the Canadian Consolidated List of Specified Persons, Economic Sanctions Lists under the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and denied-persons lists, Interpol Red Notices, and the Government of Canada's World-Check or equivalent commercial databases. Foreign public officials, their family members, and persons closely associated with senior political figures are designated as PEPs and must undergo enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring under PCMLTFA and FINTRAC expectations. The statutory UBO ownership threshold is 25%, but for this medium-risk enhanced government-affairs advisory sector FINTRAC-aligned policies should adopt a 10% control or influence threshold for PEP and high-risk jurisdiction escalation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - Registre des entreprises (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca); NUANS (Newly Updated Automated Name Search) via the Registraire's online platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names in Quebec must be in French. A French-language name must be registered before or simultaneously with any other-language version, and the legal element must appear in French or an accepted equivalent such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Limitée' or 'Incorporée'. Non-French terms are permissible only where there is no French equivalent or where the name consists of a recognized proper noun; transliteration must follow Canadian registration practice and must not create confusion with existing enterprise names in the Registre des entreprises.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Gouvernement du Québec / Government of Canada
Coopérative, Société, Mutuelle where statutory authorization is required
Any word implying Crown sponsorship, public office, or a regulated financial services activity without prior ministerial or regulatory approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registraire des entreprises rejects a name reservation, the applicant may within 30 days file a written request for reconsideration with the Registraire, attaching a revised name or additional justification and the original name-search report. If reconsideration is refused, the applicant may appeal the refusal before the Tribunal administratif du Québec under Quebec's Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. An extension of the original name reservation is not automatic; a new reservation request and search-report fee are generally required if the 90-day validity has expired.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office in Quebec must be a physical address within Quebec where service of process can be effected; a post-office box alone is prohibited. A virtual office or corporate-service-provider address is acceptable for the statutory registered office where the provider maintains a physical Quebec street address and mail receipt arrangement. For this government-affairs and lobbying advisory sector, a virtual office is sufficient for registry compliance but is not an adequate substitute for demonstrable Quebec commercial substance if employees carry on lobbying activities from Quebec; the Quebec Lobbyists Commissioner and Canada Revenue Agency may attribute permanent establishment risk where there is no physical place of operations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 30% in the first 24 months for an active registered lobbying corporation with standard UBO transparency; rising to above 50% where the registrant uses a virtual-only office, has nominee officers, or exhibits weak commercial-substance indicators. Unannounced on-site visits are uncommon absent tax or anti-money-laundering red flags, but the Registraire, Revenu Québec, and the Quebec Lobbyists Commissioner may conduct documentary inspections as part of compliance campaigns.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 9 (incorporation), 21 (articles), 110 (organization of directors); Lobbying Transparency and Ethics Act, CQLR c T-11.011, ss. 6-22 (mandatory lobbyist registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (statuts constitutifs) and Registration Statement (déclaration d'immatriculation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the QBCA for a standard share corporation; shares may be subscribed without immediate cash payment provided the corporation remains solvent. No escrow or trust account is required at incorporation; however, a corporate operating account must be opened to fund lobbying registry fees and administrative commitments.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the corporation accepts the share subscriptions set out in the Articles and issues the subscribed common shares for full consideration as fixed by the board. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at the Articles address in Quebec and the minute book and records will be kept there. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the first directors are appointed until the first annual meeting, and [Name] shall serve as Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Corporate Secretary, and [Name] as Treasurer. FURTHER RESOLVED, that management is authorized to open bank accounts and file all statutory returns, including lobbyist registration with Québec's Commissioner of Lobbying, with the Registraire des entreprises and Revenu Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online name reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name search on the REQ online database and reserve a legal name containing 'Société par actions / Inc.' or 'Corporation / Corp.' through the REQ digital portal. The name must comply with the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11). The reservation certificate is valid for 90 days and must be attached to the Articles of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Consent letter from existing entity if using a similar name
Proof of identity of the incorporating director nominee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit a revised reservation promptly; alternatively, incorporate under a numerical legal name (e.g., '12345678 Québec Inc.') without reservation, subject to later name change by amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation with the Quebec Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online incorporation portal (Société par actions / Business Corporation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and file the Articles of Incorporation electronically through the REQ digital portal. Include the corporation's legal name, registered office address in Quebec, director list, share structure (Class A common voting shares), and any restrictions. Submit the filing online and pay the registration fee by credit card. The certificate is issued electronically, and the corporation exists as of the certificate date.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation conforming to the QBCA model form
Registered office address in Quebec (physical address required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a query or notice of non-compliance, amend the Articles (statuts modificatifs) or file a supplementary declaration within the prescribed delay; corrections are effected without re-incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Organization of Directors and Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's board of directors, acting under QBCA s. 110
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the initial directors' meeting immediately after issuance of the certificate. Adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution approving share issuance, establishment of the registered office, appointment of officers, opening of bank accounts, and delegation of filing obligations. Record all decisions in the corporate minute book kept at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Acknowledgment of lobbying registration duties under the Quebec Lobbying Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the organizational resolution contains omissions, hold a subsequent directors' meeting to ratify all prior acts; any defective appointment may be cured by unanimous shareholder resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise Registration and Revenue Quebec Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The enterprise registration statement (déclaration d'immatriculation) is integrated with incorporation and must be updated within 60 days of any change. Apply to Revenu Québec for the enterprise number (NEQ), QST registration under the Act respecting the Québec sales tax, employer deductions account, and provincial income tax file. Retain proof of registration for all subsequent licensing filings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ rejects or queries the registration statement, correct and refile within 30 days; late penalties may be mitigated through voluntary disclosure and demonstration of good faith.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lobbyist Registration with the Quebec Commissioner of Lobbying
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commissaire au lobbying du Québec (Office of the Lobbying Commissioner)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before undertaking any lobbying activity with provincial public office holders, file a lobbyist registration return in the Registre des lobbyistes through the Commissioner's digital portal. Identify the corporation as the lobbyist, the subject-matter of each mandate, the public bodies to be contacted, and the responsible officer. Update the return within 30 days of any change and file annual declarations as required by law.
required_dossiers: Lobbyist registration return for each mandate
Designation of the person responsible for compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration return is rejected for incompleteness, amend and resubmit without delay; non-registration is an offence. Voluntary filing before any lobbying contact is the primary remedy and mitigates civil penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business License and Office Premises Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality (e.g., Ville de Montréal – business permit service) and local fire prevention service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business license for the registered office address, providing the lease, occupant load, and fire safety information. Obtain fire safety certification from the competent fire prevention bureau before occupancy. For an office-based advisory and lobbying practice, no environmental permit or EIA is required, but a CNESST workplace health and safety self-inspection must be documented.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of place of business
CNESST health and safety self-evaluation checklist
Landlord's structural load and occupancy confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit is withheld due to fire safety deficiencies, implement required corrective measures (portable extinguishers, exit signage), obtain a second inspection, and apply for reconsideration or an interim occupancy certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Quebec Office of the Lobbying Commissioner (Commissaire au lobbying du Québec), complemented by Revenu Québec and municipal business licensing authorities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Lobbyist registration certificate (inscription au registre des lobbyistes) under the Lobbying Transparency and Ethics Act, CQLR c T-11.011

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based professional services; no EIA report or ministerial authorization required under the Environmental Quality Act, CQLR c Q-2 for mere advisory or lobbying activities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to licensing; municipal by-law standards apply for non-process wastewater discharge, recycling and waste separation, and office ventilation; no VOC or industrial emission thresholds applicable

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local fire prevention service (exit routes, extinguishers, occupant load), structural load confirmation from the landlord or professional engineer for office lease fit-up, building occupancy permit for office use, and workplace health and safety clearance under CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA/ARC), federal income tax and national tax registry; within Quebec, Revenu Quebec (RQ) administers both the federal GST/HST and the Quebec QST under the Canada-Quebec Comprehensive Integrated Tax Coordination Agreement, as well as Quebec corporate income tax. Online portals: CRA 'My Business Account' (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency) and Revenu Quebec 'Clic Revenu / Mon dossier d'entreprise' (revenuquebec.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the Business Corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) or the Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA) and register with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec to obtain the NEQ (Numero d'entreprise du Quebec); 2) apply to CRA for the 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) via the Business Registration Online portal or Form RC1; the BN with program suffix 'RC' is the T2 corporate income tax account and with suffix 'RT' is the GST/HST account; 3) register with Revenu Quebec for GST/HST and QST accounts (combined registration) through Clic Revenu; RQ issues the QST registration number (TVQ number) and the GST registration number; 4) file the combined GST/HST and QST return (form FPZ-500) with Revenu Quebec, not CRA; 5) as a precondition of lawful fee earning, obtain and maintain registration with the federal Commissioner of Lobbying of Canada and the Quebec Lobbyists Commissioner under the Lobbying Transparency and Ethics Act, quoting the registration identifiers in commercial contracts and fee ledgers; 6) for foreign shareholders, appoint a resident agent under CBCA/QBCA and register for Part XIII withholding (NR4/NR6) or treaty-based relief filings with CRA.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary authority; banking and prudential supervision administered by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); anti-money-laundering supervision and transaction reporting governed by FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; Quebec deposit-taking cooperatives (e.g., Desjardins) are also supervised by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility in accordance with IMF Article VIII. The former Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1952; Canadian dollars are freely exchangeable without prior central bank approval. Profit remittance, dividend distributions, interest payments, and repatriation of paid-up capital by non-resident shareholders are unrestricted, subject to (i) corporate insolvency and solvency tests under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Business Corporations Act (Québec) and (ii) statutory withholding taxes under the Canada–US Income Tax Convention (generally 25% dividend rate reduced to 5%–15% for qualified US corporate shareholders). Lobbying registration requirements impose reputational and disclosure obligations, not currency restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export proceeds or service-related retainer income. Export receipts and foreign-currency consulting fees may be retained in CAD, USD, EUR, or other convertible currencies in Schedule I bank foreign-currency accounts. Reporting obligations are limited to (i) FINTRAC large cash transaction reports (net $10,000 CAD or more within 24 hours), (ii) FINTRAC international electronic funds transfer reports ($10,000 CAD or more per transaction), and (iii) CBSA cross-border currency reporting on physical movement of $10,000 CAD or more.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD/USD) plus Capital Escrow Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Montreal (BMO Bank of Montreal)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Primary operational account and Capital Escrow Account (Quebec-anchored treasury hub)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Desjardins Group (Caisse Desjardins — Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as the primary treasury rail. Wise Business, Payoneer, and Revolut Business can serve only as ancillary USD collection channels, because Canadian legal payment-service providers require registration as a foreign money services business (FMSB) under the PCMLTFA, and most international EMIs do not hold a Canadian Schedule I banking licence or CDIC deposit insurance. A Quebec-incorporated lobbying advisory with non-resident UBOs should not rely on EMIs for CAD-denominated retainer settlement or government-facing disbursements; any EMI balance must be swept to the domestic anchor bank account. Medium-risk classification (Enhanced Due Diligence) makes the fintech-only model operationally fragile.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical, in-person interview of the directing mind and at least one officer is the enforceable industry norm for Schedule I banks when onboarding a government-affairs entity with non-resident (US) stakeholders. Remote video KYC is legally permissible under FINTRAC guidance for low-risk retail relationships, but for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced lobbying corporation, the bank requires an in-branch appearance at a Quebec branch (Montréal, Québec, or Laval) or an in-person meeting with the account manager and a notarized verification of identity conducted in Canada. Remote-only onboarding is effectively denied at the High-viability tier banks absent a pre-existing private-banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry red flag: ISIC 7020 / NAICS 541820 lobbying and foreign stakeholder relations classified as elevated corruption, bribery, and public-sector-influence facade risk at account opening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Active registration certificates from the Quebec Commissaire au lobbyisme (Lobbying Register) and the federal Office of the Commissioner of Lobbying; public registry extracts naming the entity and individual lobbyists; executed client retainer agreement defining permitted policy-analysis activities; corporate charter confirming no government-employee directors in breach of Canada's five-year lobbying prohibition; written anti-bribery and political-contribution compliance policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Political Exposure (PEP) / source-of-wealth red flag: directors, officers, or any ultimate beneficial owner with prior public office, political candidacy, or close family ties to a public office holder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed PEP self-certification declarations for all UBOs and signatories; source-of-wealth memorandum with underlying asset statements and funds-trace documentation; notarized passports and proof of residential address for each director; police clearance certificates from the country of residence; three years of personal or corporate tax filings evidencing lawful income.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership opacity: US parent corporations or US individuals layered through intermediate holding entities, hindering UBO identification in the bank's beneficial-ownership register.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized corporate-chain organizational chart prepared by legal counsel; up-to-date certificate of good standing from Quebec's Registraire des entreprises and equivalents from the US state of incorporation; completed FINTRAC-compliant Beneficial Ownership Information form for every entity in the ownership chain; executed undertaking to disclose any UBO change to the bank within 15 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire activity: incoming retainer wires from foreign clients combined with outbound disbursements to international policy-research subcontractors, triggering potential sanctions-screening and trade-transparency alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully itemized invoices linked to documented lobbying registrations and engagement deliverables; underlying legislative/policy mandate documents; counterparty sanctions-screening results confirming no OFAC/EU/UN hits; tax identification numbers and regulatory profiles of all foreign clients; corporate policy prohibiting cash payments and anonymous retainer transfers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory-licence validation: failure to produce the mandatory lobbying authorization at account-opening stage may cause automatic decline due to the Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original Quebec lobbyist certificate for the entity's appointed lobbyist; updated federal lobbying return (monthly/quarterly communication reports); signed attestation of the five-year statutory ban compliance under the Lobbying Act and the Quebec Lobbying Transparency and Ethics Act; the organization's return on lobbying activities filed with the Commissioner of Lobbying in the last reporting cycle.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: US shareholder capital injection must be executed by SWIFT MT103 from the US remitting bank to the Quebec Schedule I bank account using the bank's SWIFT/BIC and the beneficiary's full corporate legal name, account number, and Quebec registered address. The wire must carry a compliant purpose code: 'EQUITY' / equity injection with a board-resolved share subscription, or 'INTRACOMPANY LOAN' with a signed promissory note if routed as shareholder debt. The receiving bank will file a FINTRAC international EFT report when the transaction equals or exceeds CAD $10,000. Supporting documents must be delivered to the bank within 10 business days of value date: board resolution authorizing issuance, share certificate ledger, corporate records, and Quebec registraire attestation; loan route additionally requires an executed interest-bearing note with arm's-length terms to avoid Quebec thin-capitalization recharacterization.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound subcontractor and international policy-research disbursements clear via (i) SWIFT MT103 bank wire for foreign counterparties and (ii) Lynx (Payments Canada's real-time gross settlement system, successor to LVTS) for domestic CAD payments among Canadian banks. Commercial letters of credit are not customary for services but may be issued for any tied goods or event-related imports; all service-based outbound wires must include an ISIC 7020 service description in remittance information, reference the underlying invoice number and lobbying registration file, and satisfy FINTRAC record-keeping. Subcontractor payments require the subcontractor's GST/HST number (and Quebec QST number where applicable) on file and a formal sub-retainer agreement to demonstrate that disbursements match legitimate service delivery.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable CAD/USD foreign-exchange forwards in the interbank market under an ISDA or IFEMA master agreement (deliverable on maturity because CAD is freely convertible)
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD) aligning USD-denominated retainer receivables with CAD operational liabilities, documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex
Vanilla CAD/USD FX options (call and put) purchased for premium-based hedge of committed retainer pipelines
FX rollovers and swap points transactions with a Canadian dealing bank for intra-month liquidity smoothing

Note: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not a permissible or market-standard instrument for CAD/USD in Canada because the Canadian dollar has an active deliverable forward market; any hedge must be supported by a documented economic exposure and board-approved treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Québec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Loi sur la publicité légale des entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following the anniversary date of the enterprise registration, on a recurring annual basis
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may generate administrative penalties; persistent non-filing may lead to cancellation of the enterprise registration and loss of corporate name protection; the corporation cannot obtain certificates of attestation and may be administratively struck off after repeated default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (for corporations incorporated or continued under the Canada Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or continuance; no obligation for a purely Quebec provincial corporation unless federal incorporation exists
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual return for at least one year may lead to dissolution of the corporation under section 212 of the CBCA; directors may be liable for debts and obligations incurred after continued non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Lobbying Registry Declaration (Déclaration annuelle du lobbyiste) under the Lobbying Transparency and Ethics Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Mandate information must be updated within 30 days of any change, and each active lobbying mandate must be confirmed or renewed on an annual basis while lobbying occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative monetary penalties and penal fines up to CAD 25,000 for individuals and CAD 50,000 for corporations per contravention; failure to register or update may result in prosecution and a negative compliance record in the Lobbyists Registry.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit for a private Quebec business corporation if all shareholders consent to waive the auditor appointment for the fiscal year. A statutory audit becomes mandatory if the corporation is a reporting issuer, distributes securities to the public, is subject to specific provincial or federal financial sector legislation, or if shareholders holding at least the statutory threshold request an audit. In practice, the audit requirement is triggered by the absence of unanimous shareholder waiver or by public-issuer status.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public/reporting issuers; private Canadian corporations may prepare financial statements under IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). Financial statements must reconcile to tax filings with Revenu Québec and the Canada Revenue Agency.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Quebec Business Corporations Act and the Canada Business Corporations Act, the corporation must maintain a register of individuals with significant control ('UBO register'). The register must be updated within 30 days of any knowledge of a change in significant control, and annually the information is confirmed as part of the annual corporate secretarial review. Share transfers are not effective against third parties until the transfer is recorded in the Register of Members, and the annual Université commercial declaration must be consistent with the UBO register and share-transfer records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (UBO Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 – 850 per year for a registered office and registered agent arrangement in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – 12,000 for a private-company certified audit; not incurred if the audit exemption is valid and no audit is demanded

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal (15%) and Quebec (11.5%) general corporate income tax; 12.2% combined on first CAD 500,000 of active business income for a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) eligible for the small business deduction
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal small business deduction (9% federal rate on taxable active business income up to CAD 500,000 for CCPCs; gradually reduced when taxable capital exceeds CAD 10 million and eliminated at CAD 15 million); Quebec small business rate (3.2% on same CAD 500,000 limit); Quebec refundable tax credits for innovation and the ‘Super-credit’ for employment of foreign talent? I'll mention: SR&ED investment tax credit (federal 35% refundable on first CAD 3 million for CCPCs; provincial), and the Quebec capital-region investment credits. Also: no statutory tax holiday for lobbying services — general corporate rate applies.
